dedupe_keys.name: cyber hil platform for ship cyber physical control systems under communication issues and cyber attacks

description: This Cyber Hardware-in-the-Loop (Cyber-HIL) platform assesses control operation in ship cyber-physical systems under communication problems and cyber attacks. It was built by Linh Vu, Tung Lam Nguyen, Mahmoud Abdelrahman, Tuyen Vu and Osama Mohammed (Clarkson University and Florida International University, with co-authors in Vietnam and Hawaii) and published in IEEE Transactions on Industry Applications in 2024, with a preprint on arXiv. The platform uses Docker containers, the OPAL-RT real-time simulator and the ns-3 network emulator to create a controlled environment for testing ship control systems. Real-time experiments used an advanced load-shedding controller of the ship power system, run synchronously and asynchronously, and evaluated it under man-in-the-middle and denial-of-service attacks on the channels between controller and simulated ship. Coverage: a generic shipboard power and control system in the laboratory. Access: the paper and preprint; the platform itself was not released. Licence and cost: the preprint is on arXiv and the journal article is closed; the platform is on request from the authors. Caveats: one controller and a laboratory ship model, with no field validation. It supports cascading failure and resilience studies of cyber attacks on vessel systems. It builds on ns-3 and OPAL-RT and resembles the SereWay railway testbed in the catalogue.
